result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides with a marked zebra crosswalk and traffic signals at the upcoming intersection. However, the pedestrian environment is constrained by narrow walkway widths, sidewalk obstructions like trash bins, and a lack of physical buffers from the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash cans and bags on the right sidewalk impede pedestrian flow and reduce effective width.

hazards.name: Narrow Effective Walkway
hazards.description: The bike share station on the left significantly reduces the available walking space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: On-Street Bike Parking
interventions.description: Relocate the bike share station from the sidewalk to the roadway to reclaim pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with continuous concrete sidewalks and row houses built directly to the property line. While the walkway is wide and unobstructed by permanent structures, significant litter and trash bags create temporary physical obstructions and tripping hazards.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Debris
hazards.description: Trash bags, cardboard, and loose litter are scattered across the sidewalk, creating tripping hazards and narrowing the effective walking width.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, center and left on the sidewalk and in the gutter.

interventions.title: Sanitation and Maintenance
interventions.description: Implement regular street cleaning and trash collection to keep the pedestrian right-of-way clear of debris.

interventions.title: Street Trees or Planters
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or large planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: The street environment provides basic pedestrian access via continuous sidewalks but lacks essential safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or traffic signals. The wide, unmarked roadway and parked vehicles create sightline obstructions and may facilitate higher vehicle speeds, increasing risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked wide roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings and wide street width can lead to unpredictable vehicle movements and higher speeds.

hazards.name: Parked vehicle sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb obscure the view between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Degraded road surface
hazards.description: Puddles and cracks in the pavement can cause pedestrians to trip or be splashed by passing vehicles.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Lane markings and narrowing
interventions.description: Paint lane lines to organize traffic and use markings to narrow the perceived travel lane, which naturally slows vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk separated from the roadway by a brick furniture zone hosting a bike-share station. While the walkway is clear and buffered, the street lacks visible crossing infrastructure, lane markings, or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No designated pedestrian crossing points are visible within the immediate street segment, which may encourage unsafe mid-block crossings.
